label: Metformin refill with a buried red flag
message: Hi, could you please renew my metformin? I have about a week of tablets left and the pharmacy said they need a new prescription. Same dose as before, 500 mg twice a day. Oh and unrelated, there's a red patch on top of my right foot that seems to be spreading since Monday, probably from my new shoes. Thanks!

questions: Do you have a fever, pain, warmth or swelling in the foot?
Do you have diabetes, and have you noticed any open sores or blisters on the foot?
Has the redness grown in size since you first noticed it?

result.justification: Flag diabetic_foot_redness: a spreading red patch on the foot in a patient who takes metformin (diabetes modifier) may be early cellulitis or a skin infection. Diabetic patients can deteriorate quickly with foot infections, so it should be assessed in person. The floor is within_few_days, but spreading redness over several days in a diabetic foot warrants a same-day exam. Not ed_now: no reported fever, severe pain, pus, black skin, red streaking, systemic symptoms or inability to walk. Not lower: waiting several days risks progression. The metformin renewal is routine, with a week of supply left, and can be handled at the same visit or alongside it.
result.safety_net: Go to the ED or call 911 right away if you develop fever or chills, red streaks moving up the leg, rapidly spreading redness, severe pain, swelling, warmth, pus, blisters, dark or black skin, numbness, vomiting, confusion, or feel very unwell. Check your blood sugar more often, and do not let your metformin run out; contact the clinic again if the refill is not sent to the pharmacy within a few days.
